correctness.rationale: PASS: For any absolutely continuous nonnegative law with F(t)>0 and finite squared normalized density on every (0,t), Cauchy–Schwarz gives (∫_0^t f/F(t))² ≤ t∫_0^t(f/F(t))², hence Jbar(t)≤−1/(2t) and Jbar(t)→−∞ as t↓0. A finite globally nonincreasing function on (0,∞) cannot have this left limit: at s<t0 it must satisfy Jbar(s)≥Jbar(t0). Publisher Theorem 2.9 has exactly the incompatible globally decreasing premise; no finite experiment is needed. The conclusion is vacuity of the characterization hypothesis, not a proof that all past-extropy monotonicity is impossible.
